name: HDFC Asset Management Company Ltd
title: HDFC Asset Management Company Ltd - 541729 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: HDFC AMC Q1 FY27: QAAUM up 13% to INR9.35tn with share 11.2%, but debt outflows and a TER-to-BER shift held yields and margins flat-to-up; no capacity or capex lever applies to this asset manager.

triggers.quote: we have seen investors redeeming from the debt funds

triggers.label: Alternatives AUM INR148bn from INR60bn
triggers.quote: Total alternatives AUM, which includes AIF commitments, portfolio management services business and advisory mandates stood at INR148 billion, up from INR60 billion a year ago.

triggers.label: Equity flows up 40% YoY
triggers.quote: equity-oriented funds saw net inflows of INR1,272 billion as compared to INR911 billion in the same quarter last year, increase of 40%

guidance.quote: We've typically operated in the 33 to 35 basis points range. And that's the objective for us to stay within that corridor.
For FY27, the total noncash cost would be around INR79 crores to INR80 crores.

summary.headline: HDFC AMC Q1 FY27: quarterly average AUM INR9.35 trillion (+13% YoY), PAT INR8.4 billion (+12% YoY), with debt AUM weakening.
summary.overview: Quarterly average AUM reached INR9.35 trillion, up 13% YoY, with market share of 11.2% (12.4% ex-ETFs). Revenue from operations rose 14% YoY to INR11 billion and PAT rose 12% YoY to INR8.4 billion. Management said margins were maintained despite a regime change from TER to BER accounting, the removal of the 5 bps exit-load-linked charge, and brokerage rationalisation from 1 April 2026. Debt QAAUM fell and debt market share was under pressure, while SIP and systematic flows kept growing.

financial_highlights.change: Equity active market share ~12.8% YoY, down ~20 bps QoQ
vs INR2.1 billion in Q1 FY26

segments.name: Equity
segments.commentary: Equity-oriented QAAUM is 65.7% of company AUM vs 56.6% for the industry; blended equity yield 58 bps. Equity market share held at around 12.8% YoY.

segments.name: Debt
segments.commentary: Debt QAAUM INR1.66 trillion with 12.9% market share; debt AUM fell about 6% QoQ on closing basis per analyst, with industry debt outflows of INR757 billion. Debt yield 28 bps.

segments.name: Liquid
segments.commentary: Liquid QAAUM INR851 billion with 10.7% market share; liquid yield 13 bps. Industry liquid inflows INR984 billion in the quarter.

segments.name: Alternatives / PMS / AIF
segments.commentary: Total alternatives AUM INR148 billion vs INR60 billion a year ago. Management says alternatives economics are slightly better than mutual fund equity; a private credit fund closes this quarter and a VC/PE fund of funds was approved with a proposed $50 million seed commitment.

guidance_outlook: Management said margins have been maintained through the new TER-to-BER regime, offset by commission optimisation and cost control; it asked not to read too much into quarterly yield movements.
Net operating margin to stay within the 33-35 bps of AUM corridor, per CFO; management will not underinvest.
Non-cash ESOP cost guided at INR79-80 crore for FY27, INR63 crore for FY28, INR41 crore for FY29 and INR11 crore for FY30.
Company declined to forecast AUM growth. Buyback vs dividend is a Board decision.
capex_capacity: Launch of first SIF offering (H-SIF equity ex top 100 long-short fund) approved by Board, launch in near term.
PMS Category 3 product in process of raising money after approval; senior resources hired for PMS and SIF.
Closing private credit fund this quarter; approval received for second fund on VC/PE side with $50 million proposed seed from a global investor.
Investment team: 37 investment professionals on mutual fund side; 6 on PE/VC, 6 on private credit, 8 on PMS (debt and equity).
demand_pricing: Industry SIP contributions INR318 billion in June 2026 vs INR273 billion in June 2025 (+17%); folios 279 million; unique investors 61.9 million.
HDFC AMC added about 0.46 million unique investors vs industry 0.53 million; base 17.1 million; penetration 28% (from 25%).
Management said fintechs registered 8.6 million SIPs (gross new registrations) in the quarter; bank channel share fell to 9.6% from 10.4% in Q1 FY26.
Debt fund outflows attributed to rupee and rate volatility, crude and geopolitics; management said industry must make debt funds more attractive to retail.
Distributor economics described as a long-term partnership; management said manufacturer-distributor economics do not change with market conditions.

qa_highlights.question: Why did debt AUM fall about 6% QoQ and why are debt outflows strong?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said investors redeemed debt funds on rupee, rate and crude volatility while liquid funds saw inflows; HDFC AMC has a decent share of both moves.

qa_highlights.question: Is the yield uptick from product mix or the TER/BER change, and what is the PMS/AIF contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it would not read too much into early-quarter movement post the accounting change. Alternatives earn 80-90 bps management fee; PMS discretionary book is in line with equity margins, non-discretionary is very tight economics.

qa_highlights.question: Has the distribution commission been rationalised and will revenue yield benefit in later quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Changes from 1 April 2026: removal of 5 bps extra TER charged in lieu of exit load, shift from TER to BER plus statutory levies, and brokerage rationalisation. Offset through commission optimisation and cost control; margins maintained.

qa_highlights.question: Why did ESOP cost jump, and is FY27 guidance unchanged?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 cost of about INR23 crore reflects a June 2025 grant under the new plan; FY27 non-cash ESOP cost guided at INR79-80 crore, unchanged at INR67 crore level per analyst reference point is for prior guide. Management said costs should be viewed annually.

qa_highlights.question: Was there an operating cost growth guidance of 12-13% ex non-cash?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said to focus on the 33-35 bps net operating margin corridor rather than quarterly cost trends.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the performance improvement in June?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited top-two-quartile performance over 2 and 3 years on AUM-weighted basis; Balance Advantage Fund in Q1 over 3, 5, 10 years, and Flexicap in Q1 over 2, 3, 5, 10 years.

risks_watch: Debt AUM outflows and debt market share pressure; management said it needs to make debt funds more attractive to retail.
Sustainability of SIP momentum and first-time investor behaviour through an extended market downturn, which management said has not yet been tested.
Distributor-channel share shifts toward fintechs; bank share fell to 9.6% from 10.4%.
Operating cost growth and rising non-cash ESOP cost; management said it will not underinvest.
Yield trajectory under the new TER-to-BER regime; management did not give forward yield guidance.
summary.management_tone: Confident on flows, structural SIP growth and long-term opportunity, but defensive and evasive on quarterly yield movements, debt outflows, CSR timing and performance questions. Management repeatedly asked analysts not to read too much into one quarter under the new regime.
key_quotes: I think the SIP flows remain very healthy for the industry.
So, what I can say is we have been able to maintain our margins.

This is like India's 401(k) movement and the investor behavior is very different than what I've seen as a fund manager or as a CIO for a long time where retail flows would ebb and flow with market sentiment.
I wouldn't like read too much into the movement in the first few months.

PMS Category 3 product raising money after approval
Private credit fund closing this quarter (alternatives AUM INR148 billion vs INR60 billion a year ago)
VC/PE fund of funds approved with proposed $50 million seed commitment

growth.why: Management declined to forecast AUM growth and guided only to a 33-35 bps operating margin corridor and ESOP costs; Q1 revenue +14% YoY and PAT +12% YoY, backed by equity inflows (+40% YoY) and new SIF/PMS/private credit/VC products, while debt AUM is weakening and no revenue guidance or capacity numbers were given.
